<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">PART I</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="Item1.Business"><!--Anchor--></a>Item 1. &#160;<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Business</font></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">General</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">We develop and manufacture small- and medium-class rockets and space systems for commercial, military and civil government customers, including the U.S. Department of Defense ("DoD"), <font style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">the National Aeronautics and Space Administration </font>("NASA") and other U.S. Government agencies. &#160;Our products and services are grouped into three reportable business segments: launch vehicles, satellites and space systems, and advanced space programs, which are described below.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left">
<table style="WIDTH: 100%; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
<tr>
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt"></td>
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol, serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top; align: right">&#183;</td>
<td style="WIDTH: auto; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Launch Vehicles - </font>Rockets that are used as small- and medium-class space launch vehicles that place satellites into Earth orbit and escape trajectories, interceptor and target vehicles for missile defense systems, and suborbital launch vehicles that place payloads into a variety of high-altitude trajectories.</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left">
<table style="WIDTH: 100%; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
<tr>
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt"></td>
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol, serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top; align: right">&#183;</td>
<td style="WIDTH: auto; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Satellites and Space Systems -</font>&#160;<font style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Small- and medium-class satellites </font>that are used to enable global and regional communications and broadcasting, conduct space-related scientific research, collect imagery and other remotely-sensed data about the Earth, carry out interplanetary and other deep-space exploration missions, and demonstrate new space technologies<font style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">.</font></td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left">
<table style="WIDTH: 100%; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
<tr>
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt"></td>
<td style="WIDTH: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol, serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top; align: right">&#183;</td>
<td style="WIDTH: auto; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Advanced Space Programs - </font>Human-rated space systems for Earth-orbit and deep-space exploration, and small- and medium-class satellites primarily used for national security space programs and to demonstrate new space technologies.</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Our general strategy is to develop and expand a core integrated business of space and launch systems technologies and products, focusing on the design and manufacture of affordable rockets, satellites and other space systems in order to establish and expand positions in niche markets that have not typically been emphasized by our larger competitors. &#160;Another part of our strategy is to seek customer contracts that will fund new product development and enhancements to our existing launch vehicle and space systems product lines. &#160;As a result of our capabilities and experience in designing, developing, manufacturing and operating a broad range of small- and medium-class rockets and space systems, we believe we are well positioned to capitalize on the demand for more affordable space-technology systems in commercial satellite communications, space-based military and intelligence operations, and missile defense programs, and to take advantage of government-sponsored initiatives in human space exploration, space-based scientific research and interplanetary exploration.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Orbital was incorporated in Delaware in 1987 to consolidate the assets, liabilities and operations of two predecessor entities established in 1982 and 1983. &#160;Our corporate headquarters are located at 45101 Warp Drive, Dulles, Virginia 20166, our telephone number is (703) 406-5000 and our website is <font style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><u>www.orbital.com</u></font>.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">&#160;</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreakArea">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageFooter">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">&#160;</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, Serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt" id="DSPFPageNumberArea">1</div>

<hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; MARGIN: 4px 0px; WIDTH: 100%; HEIGHT: 2px; COLOR: #000000; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreak" noshade="noshade">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageHeader">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS">TABLE OF CONTENTS</a></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Description of Orbital's Products and Services</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Launch Vehicles</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Our launch vehicles segment develops and produces space launch vehicles, interceptor launch vehicles and target launch vehicles.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Space Launch Vehicles</font><font style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"> - We develop and produce </font>small-class launch vehicles that place satellites weighing up to 4,000 lbs. into low-Earth orbit, including <font style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">the Pegasus, Taurus and Minotaur space launch vehicles that are used by commercial, civil government and military customers. &#160;Our Pegasus launch vehicle is launched from our L-1011 carrier aircraft to deploy relatively lightweight satellites into low-Earth orbit. &#160;The Taurus launch vehicle is a ground-launched derivative of the Pegasus vehicle that can carry heavier payloads into orbit. &#160;The ground-launched Minotaur launch vehicle family combines Minuteman II and Peacekeeper ballistic missile rocket motors with our Pegasus and Taurus technology. &#160;In 2012, we conducted one successful Pegasus launch, which deployed the Orbital-built Nuclear Spectroscopic Array Telescope satellite for NASA.</font></div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">We are nearing completion of a major product development effort to create a medium-capacity rocket, Antares, that we expect will increase the payload capacity of our space launch vehicles to approximately 14,000 lbs. for launches to low-Earth orbit. &#160;Antares will be used on our Commercial Orbital Transportation Services ("COTS") test flight and demonstration mission for NASA and under our Commercial Resupply Services ("CRS") contract with NASA to deliver cargo to the International Space Station ("ISS"). &#160;We also are marketing the vehicle to other U.S. Government and commercial customers.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Interceptor Launch Vehicles</font><font style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"> - We develop and produce r</font>ockets that are used as interceptor launch vehicles for missile defense systems, including <font style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">interceptor boosters that carry "kill vehicles" designed to defend against ballistic missile attacks. &#160;Pursuant to a contract with The Boeing Company ("Boeing"), we have been the sole supplier of operational and test interceptor boosters for the U.S. Missile Defense Agency's ("MDA") Ground-based Midcourse Defense ("GMD") program, for which our interceptor boost vehicle, a modified version of our Pegasus rocket, is being used as a major operational element in the U.S. national missile defense system. &#160;There were two deliveries of this launch vehicle during 2012. &#160;In January 2013, one of these vehicles was successfully launched as part of a test of the GMD program. &#160;With the award of the follow-on GMD development and sustainment contract in 2011, Orbital will continue to provide booster vehicles in support of the GMD program through 2018.</font></div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Target Launch Vehicles</font> - We design and produce target launch vehicles used in the development and testing of missile defense systems. &#160;Our target launch vehicles include suborbital rockets and their principal subsystems, as well as payloads carried by such vehicles. &#160;Various branches and agencies of the U.S. military, including MDA, use our target launch vehicles as targets for defense-related applications such as ballistic missile interceptor testing and related experiments. &#160;These rockets are programmed to simulate incoming enemy missiles, offering an affordable and reliable means to test advanced missile defense systems. &#160;Our family of target vehicles extends from long-range ballistic target launch vehicles, which include targets</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">for testing MDA's GMD system, to medium- and short-range target vehicles designed to simulate threats to U.S. and allied military forces deployed in overseas theaters. &#160;We have also developed a short-range supersonic sea-skimming target ("SSST") that flies just above the ocean's surface and is currently being used by the U.S. Navy. &#160;In 2012, we performed a total of three successful target missions, including a medium-range target vehicle launched in support of the MDA Aegis Ballistic Missile Defense test program and a target mission for the U.S. Army's Patriot missile defense system. &#160;We also delivered 15 SSST vehicles to the U.S. Navy in 2012.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Satellites and Space Systems</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Our satellites and space systems segment is involved in developing and producing communications satellites, science and remote sensing satellites, and related subsystems, and we also provide space technical services primarily related to scientific satellite and suborbital research rocket missions.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Communications Satellites</font><font style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"> - We design and manufacture small geosynchronous-Earth orbit ("</font>GEO") satellites that provide cable and direct-to-home television distribution, business data network connectivity, regional mobile telephony and other space-based communications services.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Science and Remote Sensing Satellites</font><font style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"> - Our small- and medium-class low-Earth orbit satellites and other spacecraft </font>are used to conduct space-related scientific research, collect imagery and other remotely-sensed data about the Earth, carry out interplanetary and other deep-space exploration missions, and demonstrate new space technologies.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">During 2012, we delivered five GEO communications satellites to commercial customers and two scientific satellites to NASA; five of these satellites were launched and placed into service in 2012, while the other two were launched in early 2013.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Space Technical Services</font> - We provide advanced space systems and subsystems, including satellite command and data handling, attitude control and structural subsystems and a broad range of space-related technical services, including analytical, engineering and manufacturing services for space-related science and defense programs. &#160;We also design, build and integrate a variety of small scientific research rockets and support field operations and launch activities for such vehicles.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Advanced Space Programs</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Our advanced space programs segment is involved in developing and producing human-rated space systems and satellites and related systems primarily used for national security space programs.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Human-Rated Space Systems</font> - We design and manufacture advanced human-rated spacecraft to be used in Earth orbit, planetary exploration and other space missions. &#160;<font style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In 2008, under the COTS research and development program, we entered into an agreement with NASA to design, build and demonstrate a new space transportation system that has the capability to deliver cargo</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">and other supplies to the ISS. &#160;This system will include a new advanced maneuvering spacecraft called Cygnus that will be launched on our Antares launch vehicle and will autonomously rendezvous with the ISS to deliver cargo to the astronauts on board. &#160;We expect the COTS demonstration mission will occur in mid-2013. &#160;Also in 2008, under the CRS program, NASA entered into a contract with us to perform eight cargo transportation missions to the ISS using the Antares/Cygnus space transportation system we are developing under our COTS program. &#160;We expect these missions to be carried out over the next four years.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">National Security Space Systems</font> -<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">&#160;</font>We develop and produce small- and medium-class satellites and related systems used primarily for national security space missions and related technology demonstration programs.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Research and Development</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We invest in product-related research and development to conceive and develop new products and to enhance existing products. &#160;Our research and development expenses totaled approximately $114.2 million, $102.8 million and $122.3 million for the years ended December 31, 2012, 2011 and 2010, respectively. &#160;</font>We believe our research and development expenses will decline in 2013 as we are nearing completion of our Antares and COTS development programs.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Patents and Proprietary Rights</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">We rely in part on patents, trade secrets and know-how to develop and maintain our competitive position and technological advantage, particularly with respect to our launch vehicle and satellite products. &#160;While our intellectual property rights in the aggregate are important to the operation of our business, we do not believe that any single existing patent or other intellectual property right is of such importance that its loss or termination would have a material adverse effect on our business, taken as a whole.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Components and Raw Materials; Seasonality</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">We purchase a significant percentage of our subassemblies and instruments from domestic and foreign suppliers. &#160;We also obtain from the U.S. Government parts and equipment that are used in the production of our products or in the provision of our services. &#160;Generally, we have not experienced material difficulty in obtaining product components or necessary parts and equipment and we believe that alternatives to our existing sources of supply are available in most cases, although we could incur increased costs and possible delays in securing alternative sources of supply.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">We rely upon sole-source suppliers for most solid-propellant rocket motors and liquid-propellant rocket engines used on our launch vehicles. &#160; For example, our Antares launch vehicle uses liquid-propellant AJ-26 engines, which are modified Russian rocket engines, for its first stage that is available solely from one supplier. &#160;These engines are no longer in production, and while there is sufficient quantity of these engines to complete the CRS and COTS programs, there is a limited supply available for other potential missions. &#160;While we believe that alternative sources for rocket motors and engines would be available, the inability of our current suppliers to provide us with rocket motors and engines, such as the AJ-26, could result in significant contract delays, cost increases and loss of revenues due to the time, resources and effort that would be required to develop or adapt other engines or motors for use in our products.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Our business is not seasonal.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">U.S. Government Contracts</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">During 2012, 2011 and 2010, approximately 79%, 71% and 74%, respectively, of our total annual revenues were derived from contracts with the U.S. Government and its agencies or from subcontracts with other U.S. Government contractors. &#160;Most of our U.S. Government contracts are funded incrementally on a year-to-year basis.</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreakArea">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageFooter">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">&#160;</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, Serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt" id="DSPFPageNumberArea">6</div>

<hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; MARGIN: 4px 0px; WIDTH: 100%; HEIGHT: 2px; COLOR: #000000; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreak" noshade="noshade">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageHeader">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS">TABLE OF CONTENTS</a></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Our major contracts with the U.S. Government primarily fall into two categories: cost-reimbursable contracts and fixed-price contracts. &#160;Approximately 58% and 42% of our revenues from U.S. Government contracts in 2012 were derived from cost-reimbursable contracts and fixed-price contracts, respectively. &#160;Under cost-reimbursable contracts, we recover our actual allowable costs incurred, allocable indirect costs and a fee consisting of (i) a base amount that is fixed at the inception of the contract and/or (ii) an award amount that is based on the customer's evaluation of our performance in terms of the criteria stated in the contract. &#160;Our fixed-price contracts include firm fixed-price and fixed-price incentive fee contracts. &#160;Under firm fixed-price contracts, work performed and products shipped are paid for at a fixed price without adjustment for actual costs incurred in connection with the contract. &#160;Therefore, we bear the risk of loss if costs increase, although some of this risk may be passed on to subcontractors. &#160;Fixed-price incentive fee contracts provide for sharing by us and the customer of unexpected costs incurred or savings realized within specified limits, and may provide for adjustments in price depending on actual contract performance other than costs. &#160;Costs in excess of the negotiated maximum (ceiling) price and the risk of loss by reason of such excess costs are borne by us, although some of this risk may be passed on to subcontractors.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">As noted above, we derive a significant portion of our revenues from U.S. Government contracts, which are dependent on continued political support and funding. &#160;All our U.S. Government contracts and, in general, our subcontracts with other U.S. Government prime contractors provide that such contracts may be terminated for convenience at any time by the U.S. Government or the prime contractor, respectively. &#160;Furthermore, any of these contracts may become subject to a government-issued stop work order under which we would be required to suspend production. &#160;In the event of a termination for convenience, contractors generally are entitled to receive the purchase price for delivered items, reimbursement for allowable costs for work in process and an allowance for reasonable profit thereon or adjustment for loss if completion of performance would have resulted in a loss. &#160;For a more detailed description of risks relating to the U.S. Government contract industry, see "Item 1A</font> &#8211; <font style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Risk Factors."</font></div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">A portion of our business is classified for national security purposes by the U.S. Government and cannot be specifically described. &#160;The operating results of these classified programs are included in our consolidated financial statements. &#160;The business risks associated with classified programs, as a general matter, do not differ materially from those of our other U.S. Government contracts, and are subject to the same operational, compliance and financial reporting controls.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Regulation</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Our ability to pursue our business activities is regulated by various agencies and departments of the U.S. Government and, in certain circumstances, the governments of other countries. &#160;Commercial space launches require licenses from the U.S. Department of Transportation ("DoT") and the reentry of our Cygnus maneuvering spacecraft during the COTS demonstration mission and the operation of our L-1011 aircraft require licenses from certain agencies of the DoT, including the Federal Aviation Administration ("FAA"). &#160;The use of the AJ-26 engine, which is a modified Russian rocket engine, on our Antares rocket requires a Russian government license, which we have obtained for our missions currently under contract. &#160;The Federal Communications Commission ("FCC") also requires licenses for radio communications during our rocket launches. &#160;Our classified programs require that we and certain of our employees maintain appropriate security clearances. &#160;We also require export licenses from the U.S. Department of State ("DoS"), the U.S. Department of Commerce ("DoC") and, occasionally, the governments of other countries with respect to transactions we have with foreign customers or foreign subcontractors.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Contract Backlog</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Our firm backlog was approximately $2.20 billion at December 31, 2012 and approximately $2.39<font style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">&#160;</font>billion at December 31, 2011. &#160;While there can be no assurance, we expect to convert approximately $940 million of the 2012 year-end firm backlog into revenues during 2013. &#160;Our firm backlog as of December 31, 2012 included approximately $2.0 billion of contracts with the U.S. Government and its agencies or from subcontracts with prime contractors of the U.S. Government. &#160;Most of our U.S. Government contracts are funded incrementally on a year-to-year basis. &#160;Firm backlog from U.S. Government contracts at December 31, 2012 included total funded orders of about $670<font style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">&#160;</font>million and orders not yet funded of about $1.33 billion. &#160;Changes in government policies, priorities or funding levels through agency or program budget reductions by the U.S. Congress or executive agencies could materially adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations. &#160;Furthermore, contracts with the U.S. Government may be terminated or suspended by the U.S. Government at any time, with or without cause, which could result in a reduction in backlog.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Total backlog was approximately $5.03 billion at December 31, 2012. &#160;Total backlog includes firm backlog in addition to unexercised options, indefinite-quantity contracts and undefinitized orders and contract award selections.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="Item1A.RiskFactors"><!--Anchor--></a>Item 1A. &#160;<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Risk Factors</font></div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Investors should carefully consider, among other factors, the risks listed below.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">We derive a significant portion of our revenues from U.S. Government contracts, which are dependent on continued political support and funding and are subject to termination by the U.S. Government at any time.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">The majority of our total annual revenues and our firm backlog at December 31, 2012 were derived from U.S. Government contracts. &#160;Most of our U.S. Government contracts are funded incrementally on a year-to-year basis and are subject to uncertain future funding levels. &#160;Our direct and indirect contracts with the U.S. Government may be terminated or suspended by the U.S. Government or its prime contractors at any time, with or without cause. &#160;Termination or suspension of any of our significant U.S. Government contracts could result in the loss of future revenues and unreimbursable expenses or charges that could have a materially adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations. &#160;Furthermore, key human space initiatives, missile defense programs, and other space programs must compete with other programs for consideration during the federal budgeting and appropriation process, and support and funding for any U.S. Government program may be influenced by general economic conditions, political considerations and other factors. &#160;A decline in U.S. Government support and funding for programs in which we participate could result in contract terminations, delays in contract awards, the failure to exercise contract options, the cancellation of planned procurements and fewer new</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">In particular, the Budget Control Act of 2011 commits the U.S. Government to significantly reduce the federal deficit over ten years through caps on discretionary spending and other measures, including automatic across-the-board spending cuts through the sequestration process, if necessary. &#160;Such spending cuts would be split equally between defense and non-defense programs over a ten-year period. &#160;Although the American Taxpayer Relief Act of 2012 has delayed sequestration temporarily, without further action, it will take effect on March 1, 2013. &#160;It remains uncertain whether the contemplated sequester will take place or if it will be delayed, modified or averted. &#160;Any automatic across-the-board cuts required by sequestration would affect Orbital's U.S. Government customers, in particular, DoD and NASA.&#160;&#160;While the impact of sequestration on our individual U.S. Government programs is unclear, funding for programs in which we participate or new contract awards that we seek to win could be reduced, delayed or cancelled. &#160;As a result, our business, financial condition and results of operations could be materially adversely affected. &#160;Even if sequestration does not occur, our U.S. Government customers could face some level of spending cuts, which could adversely impact our business, financial condition and results of operation.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">We are subject to a number of domestic and international laws, regulations and restrictions, the non-compliance with which may expose us to adverse consequences.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">As a government contractor, we are subject to extensive and complex U.S. Government procurement laws and regulations, including the Procurement Integrity Act and the False Claims Act. &#160;Failure to comply with these laws and regulations could result in contract termination, price or fee reductions, civil or criminal penalties, injunctions and/or administrative sanctions such as suspension or debarment from contracting with the U.S. Government.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">In addition, our international business subjects us to numerous U.S. and foreign laws and regulations, including the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act and regulations relating to import-export control. &#160;Our failure to comply with these laws and regulations could result in administrative, civil or criminal penalties and administrative sanctions such as suspension or debarment from contracting with the U.S. Government or suspension of our export privileges, which could result in the termination of existing U.S. Government contracts, affect our ability to win new U.S. Government contracts, and impair our ability to serve foreign customers.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Our business could be adversely affected by adverse audit findings by the U.S. Government.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">U.S. Government agencies, including the Defense Contract Audit Agency and various agency Inspectors General, routinely audit and investigate government contractors. &#160;These agencies review a contractor's performance under its contracts, cost structure and compliance with applicable laws, regulations and standards. &#160;Charging practices relating to labor, research and development, and other costs that may be charged directly or indirectly to U.S. Government contracts are often scrutinized to determine that such costs are allowable under U.S. Government contracts and furthermore that such costs are reasonable. &#160;Any costs determined to be unallowable or unreasonable may not be reimbursed, and such costs already reimbursed may be</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Overview</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Introduction</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Orbital Sciences Corporation develops and manufactures small- and medium-class rockets and space systems for commercial, military and civil government customers. &#160;Our primary products and services include the following:</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div>
<table style="WIDTH: 100%; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" class="DSPFListTable" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
<tr>
<td style="WIDTH: 36pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top; align: right">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol, serif; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">&#183;</div>
</td>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Our general strategy is to develop and expand a core integrated business of space and launch system technologies and products, focusing on the design and manufacture of affordable rockets, satellites and other space systems in order to establish and expand positions in niche markets that have not typically been emphasized by our larger competitors. &#160;Another part of our strategy is to seek customer contracts that will fund new product development and enhancements to our existing launch vehicle and space systems product lines. &#160;As a result of our capabilities and experience in designing, developing, manufacturing and operating a broad range of small- and medium-class rockets and space systems, we believe we are well positioned to capitalize on the demand for more affordable space-technology systems in commercial satellite communications, space-based military and intelligence operations and military defense programs, and to take</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-STYLE: italic; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Business and Industry Considerations</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">U.S. Government Business - </font>During 2012, 2011 and 2010, approximately 79%, 71% and 74%, respectively, of our consolidated revenues were derived from contracts with the U.S.&#160;Government and its agencies or from subcontracts with other U.S.&#160;Government contractors. &#160;Most of our U.S.&#160;Government contracts are funded incrementally on a year-to-year basis. &#160;As a result, our operations and our financial results in any period could be impacted substantially by trends in U.S. Government spending, shifting priorities in DoD (including MDA), NASA and other agency budgets, the types of contracts and payment terms mandated by the U.S. Government and changes in the Executive Branch and Congress. &#160;These factors, which are largely beyond our control, could have a significant impact on our business.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">The Budget Control Act of 2011 commits the U.S. Government to significantly reduce the federal deficit over ten years through caps on discretionary spending and other measures, including automatic across-the-board spending cuts through the sequestration process, if necessary. &#160;Although Congress has delayed sequestration temporarily, without further action, it will take effect on March 1, 2013. &#160;It remains uncertain whether the contemplated sequester will take place, or if it will be delayed, modified or averted. &#160;In general, we expect that our U.S. Government customers will experience reductions in their budgets compared to recent levels. &#160;Such reductions could occur even if a compromise is reached on U.S. Government spending and sequestration is averted.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">NASA continues to prioritize funding for development of U.S. commercial cargo and crew services for the International Space Station. &#160;Accordingly, funding for our COTS demonstration mission, including an Antares test launch, and our CRS contract currently remains unaffected by budget cuts. &#160; Priorities with respect to Earth and space science investigations are less clear, but we believe the NASA budget for these programs could be reduced as a result of a focus on other programs, which could have a negative impact on certain of our current programs or potential future pursuits.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">The majority of Orbital's missile defense interceptor and target launch vehicle revenues comes from programs sponsored by MDA. &#160;The Budget Control Act of 2011 provides for a significant reduction in defense budgets over a ten-year period, with further reductions possible in the event of sequestration. &#160; Consequently, we expect federal spending on space and missile defense programs to be lower compared to historical levels over the next couple of years. &#160;Due to uncertainties regarding funding and federal budgets, we believe certain MDA programs could be delayed or reduced in scope.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">We believe that federal budget constraints may impact national security space programs, possibly resulting in program delays, cancellations or scope reductions. &#160;DoD and the intelligence community have for some missions historically relied on large multi-mission space systems that are very expensive and require a decade or longer to be built and deployed. &#160;We believe that DOD and the intelligence community are considering ways to address their</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreakArea">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageFooter">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">&#160;</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, Serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt" id="DSPFPageNumberArea">27</div>

</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">operational requirements on more limited budgets by considering smaller and more affordable space systems that we believe are within our addressable market; however, it is uncertain whether we will achieve any competitive advantages as a result.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Commercial Satellites Business </font>- Our largest commercial business is the design and manufacture of <font style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">small-class GEO </font>communications satellites. &#160;Commercial communications satellites accounted for 21%, 29% and 26% of our consolidated revenues in 2012, 2011 and 2010, respectively.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">The commercial communications satellite market is driven by economic conditions that may affect satellite operators directly as well as their satellite replacement requirements. &#160;In 2012, the total number of commercial GEO satellite orders was similar to the number ordered in 2011, as the largest satellite operators continued their trend of reduced capital spending, following greater expenditures in prior years. &#160;We expect capital spending from the major satellite operators to remain at similarly low levels in the near future. &#160;As a result, we expect that the total number of commercial GEO satellite orders placed in 2013, including the number of satellite orders in our addressable market, will be comparable to those of 2011 and 2012.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Critical Accounting Policies and Significant Estimates</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">The preparation of consolidated financial statements requires management to make judgments based upon estimates and assumptions that are inherently uncertain. &#160;Such judgments affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenues and expenses, and related disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities. &#160;Management continuously evaluates its estimates and assumptions, including those related to long-term contracts and incentives, inventories, long-lived assets, income taxes, contingencies and litigation, and the carrying values of assets and liabilities. &#160;Management bases its estimates on historical experience and on various other assumptions that it believes to be reasonable under the circumstances. &#160;Actual results may differ from these estimates under different assumptions or conditions, and such differences may be material.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">The following is a summary of the most critical accounting policies used in the preparation of our consolidated financial statements.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Revenue Recognition</font> - Our revenues are derived primarily from long-term contracts. &#160;Revenues on long-term contracts are recognized using the percentage-of-completion method of accounting. &#160;Such revenues are recorded based on the percentage that costs incurred to date bear to the most recent estimates of total costs to complete each contract. &#160;Estimating future revenues, costs and profit is a process requiring a high degree of management judgment, including management's assumptions regarding our future operational performance as well as general economic conditions. &#160;In the event of a change in total estimated contract revenue, cost or profit, the cumulative effect of such change is recorded in the period the change in estimate occurs. &#160;Frequently, the period of performance of a contract extends over a long period of time and, as such, revenue recognition and our profitability from a particular contract may be adversely affected to the extent that estimated costs to complete or incentive or award fee estimates are revised, delivery schedules are delayed, performance-based milestones are not achieved or</div>

<div style="MARGIN-TOP: 10pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 10pt; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreakArea">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageFooter">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">&#160;</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, Serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt" id="DSPFPageNumberArea">28</div>

<hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; MARGIN: 4px 0px; WIDTH: 100%; HEIGHT: 2px; COLOR: #000000; CLEAR: both" id="DSPFPageBreak" noshade="noshade">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageHeader">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS">TABLE OF CONTENTS</a></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">progress under a contract is otherwise impeded. &#160;Accordingly, our recorded revenues and operating profit from period to period can fluctuate significantly. &#160;In the event cost estimates indicate a loss on a contract, the total amount of such loss, excluding general and administrative expense, is recorded in the period in which the loss is first estimated.</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Many of our contracts include provisions that increase or decrease contract value based on performance in relation to established targets or customer evaluations. &#160;Mission success milestones and incentive and award fees are included in estimated contract revenue when we are able to make reasonable predictions about whether the performance targets will be achieved and make dependable estimates of such amounts based upon our historical experience with similar types of activities and other objective criteria. &#160;We include the estimated amount of mission success milestones and incentive and award fees in estimated contract revenue at the inception of each contract, with reassessments made each quarter throughout the period of contract performance. &#160;If performance under such contracts were to differ from previous assumptions, or if we were to revise our estimates or assumptions, current period revenues and profit would be adjusted and could fluctuate significantly. &#160;Our assessments are guided by the historical performance of our products and product families, the reliability record of the technology employed and assessments of technological considerations for each contract.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">As part of our risk management strategy, we generally insure significant mission success milestone receipts. &#160;Insurance recoveries are recorded as other income in the consolidated financial statements.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Mission success milestones relating to the launch of our Antares rocket with its Cygnus payload and the successful delivery of cargo to the ISS comprise approximately 25% of total CRS contract value. &#160;If we do not achieve these mission success milestones, we may be required to record revenue and profit reductions. &#160;Since the inception of the CRS contract in December 2008 through December 31, 2012, we have recognized $974 million of revenues on the contract, which has a total contract value of approximately $1.9 billion.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">As of December 31, 2012, unbilled receivables included approximately $9 million of incentive fees on certain completed satellite contracts that become due incrementally over periods of up to 15 years, subject to the achievement of performance criteria.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Certain satellite contracts require the company to refund a portion of the contract price to the customer if performance criteria, which cover periods of up to 15 years, are not<font style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"> satisfied. &#160;As of December 31, 2012, we could be required to refund up to approximately $12 million to customers if certain completed satellites were to fail to satisfy performance criteria. &#160;We </font>generally procure insurance policies under which we believe we would recover satellite incentive fees that are not earned and potential performance refund obligations.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Research and Development</font> - Expenditures for company-sponsored research and development projects are expensed as incurred. &#160;Research and development projects performed under contracts for customers are recorded as contract costs. &#160;In 2008, we entered into the COTS agreement with NASA to design, build and demonstrate a new space transportation system for delivering cargo and supplies to the ISS. &#160;The COTS agreement is accounted for as a best-efforts</div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageFooter">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">&#160;</div>
</div>

</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">research and development cost-sharing arrangement. &#160;As such, the amounts funded by NASA are recognized proportionally as an offset to our COTS program research and development expenses, including associated general and administrative expenses.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Income Taxes</font> - We account for income taxes using the asset and liability method. &#160;Under this method, deferred tax assets and liabilities are recorded for the future tax consequences attributable to differences between the financial statement carrying amounts of assets and liabilities and their respective tax bases. &#160;Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. &#160;The effect of a tax rate change on deferred tax assets and liabilities is recognized in income in the period that includes the enactment date. &#160;We record valuation allowances to reduce net deferred tax assets to the amount considered more likely than not to be realized. &#160;Changes in estimates of future taxable income can materially change the amount of such valuation allowances.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Consolidated Results of Operations for the Years Ended December 31, 2012, 2011 and 2010</div>

<div><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Revenues</font> - Our consolidated revenues were $1,436.8 million in 2012, an increase of $90.8 million, or 7%, compared to 2011 due to higher revenues in the launch vehicles segment and advanced space programs segment partially offset by lower revenues in the satellites and space systems segment. &#160;Launch vehicles segment revenues increased $44.1 million, or 9%, in 2012 primarily due to increased activity on target launch vehicle contracts, partially offset by decreased activity on missile defense interceptors and lower space launch vehicle revenues. &#160;In addition, 2011 revenues in the launch vehicles segment were reduced by an $11.3 million adjustment as a result of a Taurus XL launch failure in March 2011. &#160;Advanced space programs segment revenues increased $36.1 million, or 8%, in 2012 primarily due to increased activity on the CRS contract partially offset by decreased activity on national security satellite contracts. &#160;Satellites and space systems segment revenues decreased $57.6 million, or 10%, in 2012 due to lower activity on communications satellite contracts that were completed or substantially completed in 2012, partially offset by higher activity on space technical services contracts and science and remote sensing satellite contracts.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Eliminations of intersegment revenues decreased to $56.8 million in 2012 compared to $125.1 million in 2011. &#160;Intersegment revenues included $47.6 million and $114.4 million in 2012 and 2011, respectively, pertaining to Antares launch vehicle production work reported in our launch vehicles segment as part of the COTS program that is reported in our advanced space programs segment. &#160;Antares production work on the COTS program decreased significantly as the COTS program was nearing completion in late 2012.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">The CRS contract accounted for 24% and 18% of consolidated revenues in 2012 and 2011, respectively. &#160;The launch vehicle portion of the CRS contract is reported in our launch vehicles segment and the remainder of the CRS contract is reported in our advanced space programs segment. &#160;CRS contract revenues totaled $345.9 million in 2012, an increase of $98.5 million, or 40%, compared to 2011, due to increased production activity. &#160;Since the inception of the CRS contract through December 31, 2012, a total of $974 million of revenues have been recognized on the contract, which has a total contract value of approximately $1.9 billion.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Our consolidated revenues were $1,345.9 million in 2011, an increase of $51.3 million, or 4%, compared to 2010 due to higher revenues in all business segments. &#160;Satellites and space systems segment revenues increased $56.8 million, or 11%, in 2011 due to increased activity on communications satellite contracts and space technical services contracts, partly offset by lower activity on science and remote sensing satellite contracts. &#160; Launch vehicles segment revenues increased $48.7 million, or 11%, in 2011 primarily due to increased activity on target launch vehicle and space launch vehicle contracts, partly offset by decreased activity on missile defense interceptor contracts. &#160;Advanced space programs segment revenues increased $10.4 million, or 2%, in 2011 primarily due to increased activity on national security satellite contracts, partially offset by a decrease in activity on the Orion contract, which was terminated for convenience in the second quarter of 2010, and decreased activity on the CRS contract.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Eliminations of intersegment revenues increased to $125.1 million in 2011 compared to $60.6 million in 2010. &#160;Intersegment revenues included $114.4 million and $51.8 million in 2011 and 2010, respectively, pertaining to Antares launch vehicle production work in our launch vehicles segment for the COTS program that is reported in our advanced space programs segment.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Cost of Revenues </font>- Our cost of revenues was $1,097.2 million in 2012, an increase of $22.8 million, or 2%, compared to 2011. &#160;Cost of revenues includes the cost of personnel, materials, subcontractors and overhead. &#160; Cost of revenues in the advanced space programs segment increased $27.4 million, or 8%, primarily due to higher contract costs on the CRS program. &#160;Cost of revenues in the launch vehicles segment increased $6.6 million, or 2%, which was lower than the revenue increase in this segment largely due to the effect of the 2011 revenue reduction resulting from the March 2011 launch failure mentioned above. &#160;Cost of revenues in the satellites and space systems segment decreased $79.5 million, or 17%, primarily due to lower production activity and reduced materials and subcontract costs on communications satellite contracts. &#160; &#160;Eliminations of intersegment cost of revenues decreased $68.3 million in 2012 attributable to the decrease in intersegment revenues discussed above.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Our cost of revenues was $1,074.4 million in 2011, an increase of $66.7 million, or 7%, compared to 2010. &#160;The increase in cost of revenues was principally due to an increased level of subcontract activity and materials purchases that were generally consistent with the consolidated revenue increase discussed above. &#160;Cost of revenues in the launch vehicles segment increased $73.4 million, or 22%, in 2011 compared to 2010, which exceeded the revenue increase in this segment largely due to the 2011 revenue reduction resulting from the 2011 launch failure mentioned above. &#160;Cost of revenues in the satellites and space systems segment increased $48.5 million, or 11%, in 2011. &#160;Cost of revenues in the advanced space programs segment increased $9.3 million, or 3%, in 2011. &#160;Eliminations of intersegment cost of revenues increased $64.5 million in 2011 attributable to the increase in intersegment revenues discussed above.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Research and Development Expenses</font> - Our research and development expenses totaled $114.2 million, or 8% of revenues, in 2012, an $11.4 million increase compared to $102.8 million, or 8% of revenues, in 2011. &#160;The increase in research and development expenses was primarily attributable to product enhancements in the satellites and space systems segment and increased costs pertaining to the Antares launch vehicle development program. &#160;These factors</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">The COTS program is accounted for as a best-efforts research and development cost-sharing arrangement. &#160;As such, the amounts funded by NASA are recognized proportionally as an offset to the company's COTS program research and development expenses, including associated general and administrative expenses. &#160;Under the COTS agreement, as amended, as of December 31, 2012, NASA has agreed to pay us $288 million in cash milestone payments, partially funding our program costs which are currently estimated to be approximately $513 million. &#160;We expect to complete this program in the first half of 2013. &#160;The following table summarizes the COTS program costs incurred and amounts funded by NASA recorded in research and development expenses (<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">in millions</font>):</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Research and development expenses attributable to our Antares launch vehicle development program were $42.6 million, $34.3 million and $48.3 million in 2012, 2011 and 2010, respectively.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">We believe that the majority of our research and development expenses are recoverable and billable under our contracts with the U.S. Government. &#160;Charging practices relating to research and development and other costs that may be charged directly or indirectly to government contracts are subject to audit by U.S. Government agencies to determine if such costs are reasonable and allowable under government contracting regulations and accounting practices. &#160;We believe that the research and development costs incurred in connection with our Antares development program are allowable, although the U.S. Government has not yet made a final determination. &#160;During 2012, 2011 and 2010, we incurred $42.6 million, $34.3 million and $43.2 million, respectively, of such expenses that have been recorded as allowable costs. &#160;Since the inception of the Antares program through December 31, 2012, we have incurred $196.1 million of such costs. &#160;If such costs were determined to be unallowable, we could be required to record revenue and profit reductions in future periods.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">In 2010, we established a self-imposed ceiling on the amount of research and development expenses that we would recover under our U.S. Government contracts. &#160;Although we believe that such expenses would otherwise have been allowable and recoverable under government contracting regulations and accounting practices, in 2010, we incurred $5.1 million of research and development costs in excess of our self-imposed ceiling for which we did not seek recovery under our U.S. Government contracts.</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Selling, General and Administrative Expenses </font>- Selling, general and administrative expenses were $112.8 million, $89.0 million and $91.6 million in 2012, 2011 and 2010, respectively, or 8%, 7% and 7% of revenues, respectively. &#160;Selling, general and administrative expenses include the cost of our finance, legal, administrative and general management functions, as well as bid, proposal and marketing costs.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Selling, general and administrative expenses increased $23.8 million, or 27%, in 2012 compared to 2011 primarily due to an increase in bid, proposal and marketing costs pertaining to new business pursuits in the advanced space programs segment and launch vehicles segment, and due to an increase in certain corporate-level professional fees and expenses. &#160;In addition, selling, general and administrative expenses in 2012 included $2.1 million of professional fees and other costs related to a potential acquisition that was not consummated.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Selling, general and administrative expenses decreased $2.6 million, or 3%, in 2011 compared to 2010 primarily due to a decrease in bid, proposal and marketing costs in all of our business segments and the absence of $1.6 million of transaction expenses incurred in 2010 in connection with a business acquisition.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Operating Income -</font> Our consolidated operating income was $112.6 million in 2012, an increase of $32.8 million, or 41%, compared to 2011 due to higher operating income in all three operating business segments. &#160;Launch vehicles segment operating income increased $22.0 million, or 155%, largely due to an adjustment that reduced 2011 operating income by $11.3 million in connection with the March 2011 rocket launch failure mentioned above and increased operating income from the CRS and target launch vehicle contracts. &#160;<font style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">S</font>atellites and space systems segment operating income increased $8.6 million, or 23%, primarily due to profit improvements on certain communications satellite contracts that were substantially completed in 2012 and a $6.5 million contract settlement charge that reduced operating income in 2011. &#160;Advanced space programs segment operating income increased $4.3 million, or 15%, primarily due to a favorable contract closeout adjustment in 2012 in addition to increased activity on the CRS contract, partially offset by decreased activity on national security satellite contracts. &#160;Operating income in 2012 was reduced by $2.1 million of unallocated professional fees and other costs, recorded in corporate and other, related to a potential acquisition that was not consummated.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Total operating income from the CRS contract was $16.7 million in 2012, an increase of $4.2 million, or 34%. &#160;Since the inception of the CRS program through December 31, 2012, a total of $48 million of operating income has been recognized on the program.</div>

<div style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Our consolidated operating income was $79.8 million in 2011, an increase of $6.8 million, or 9%, compared to 2010 due to higher operating income in the advanced space programs segment and the satellites and space systems segment partially offset by lower operating income in the launch vehicles segment. &#160;Advanced space programs segment operating income increased $7.0 million, or 33%, primarily due to increased activity on national security satellite contracts. &#160;<font style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; COLOR: #000000; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">S</font>atellites and space systems segment operating income increased $3.8 million, or 11%, primarily due to increased activity on communications satellite contracts partially offset by decreased activity on science and remote sensing satellite contracts. &#160;Launch vehicles segment operating income decreased $7.0 million, or 33%, primarily due to the effect of the 2011 launch failure,</div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%" id="DSPFPageFooter">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">&#160;</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman', Times, Serif; FONT-SIZE: 12pt" id="DSPFPageNumberArea">33</div>
